sources.title: Sascha Friedli and Yvan Velenik, Statistical Mechanics of Lattice Systems: A Concrete Mathematical Introduction (complete author-hosted book, revised 2017)
sources.locator: Chapter 3, §3.1, finite-volume Ising distributions with fixed boundary conditions, printed pp. 80–82 (PDF pp. 97–99); Chapter 6, §6.5.2, Theorem 6.31, equations (6.37)–(6.40), Lemma 6.34 and its proof, and Proposition 6.33 and its proof, printed pp. 268–271 (PDF pp. 285–288).

contents.name: Definition 3.3: finite-volume Ising Gibbs distribution with fixed boundary

source_review.read_extent: The finite-volume conditional energy and normalized Gibbs weights in §3.1 were read at printed pp. 81–82.
source_review.supports: The finite Ising Gibbs weights and fixed-boundary finite-volume convention used by the local finite-response derivation.
source_review.limitations: The local response lemma differentiates finite normalized sums itself; no derivative identity is borrowed from this definition.

contents.name: Finite Gibbs response of an observable to a field-coupled observable

source_review.read_extent: The source's finite Gibbs weights were read in §3.1; the local lemma's numerator and denominator derivatives are established directly from finite sums.
source_review.supports: The finite normalized Gibbs family and its field-coupled observable setting.
source_review.limitations: The general covariance derivative is the complete local proof in this item, not a quoted or assumed source theorem.

contents.name: Dobrushin one-site coefficients, row criterion, and oscillations (equations (6.37)–(6.40))

source_review.read_extent: The coefficient definition, the row-sum criterion, and the oscillation definition were read in full at equations (6.37)–(6.40).
source_review.supports: The one-site influence-matrix definition and the role of finite coordinate oscillations.
source_review.limitations: The book's coefficient uses the full sum of absolute probability differences; the local definition explicitly uses half total variation, so its coefficients are one half of the book's displayed convention.

source_review.read_extent: Theorem 6.31 and its uniqueness proof, including Proposition 6.33 and Lemma 6.34 with proof, were read in §6.5.2, printed pp. 268–270 (PDF pp. 285–287). Section 6.12.2 was checked and identified as the proof of Theorem 6.5, so it is not cited for this result.
source_review.supports: The qualitative uniqueness consequence and the role of boundary sensitivity.
source_review.limitations: The new comparison theorem proves its own quantitative two-specification estimate; Theorem 6.31 is used only for existence and uniqueness of the states under the single-specification hypotheses.

contents.name: Oscillation after a one-site conditional update (Lemma 6.34, dusting lemma)
contents.reason: The local comparison proof uses finite-volume coupled heat-bath chains and a matrix resolvent; the source's separate dusting iteration is not needed as a premise or proof step.

contents.name: Repeated dusting contracts the difference of two Gibbs states (Proposition 6.33)
contents.reason: This is a separate qualitative uniqueness proof route. The assigned quantitative two-kernel comparison estimate is proved locally by stationary finite-volume coupling and is not replaced by this iteration.

sources.title: Patrick Rebeschini and Ramon van Handel, Comparison Theorems for Gibbs Measures
sources.locator: §§2.1–2.3, Theorem 2.4 and Corollary 2.6; §§3.1–3.3, coupled-update comparison principle and proof, PDF pp. 4–9 and 12–23.

contents.name: Classical Dobrushin comparison bound with Neumann resolvent (Corollary 2.6)

source_review.read_extent: The complete single-site corollary statement, its total-variation specialization, and its resolvent $D=\sum_{n\geq0}C^n$ were read in §2.3.
source_review.supports: The claimed functional comparison bound in terms of oscillations, local discrepancies, and the Dobrushin resolvent.
source_review.limitations: The local theorem states a uniform pointwise discrepancy and proves both finite-volume boundary and infinite DLR forms directly; it does not rely on the paper's regularity or outer-integral machinery.

contents.name: Coupled-update comparison principle and Gibbs-sampler proof route (Theorem 2.4; §§3.1–3.3)

source_review.read_extent: The Gibbs-sampler construction, oscillation comparison lemma, finite iteration estimate, and limiting resolvent argument were read in the proof sections.
source_review.supports: The finite-volume common-update coupling strategy and the use of a nonnegative Neumann series.
source_review.limitations: The item gives its own complete finite-state stationary-coupling proof, including the measurable finite-boundary-pattern selection needed for DLR integration.
